input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us (bespoke reports, configurations, integrations, designs and workflows under the definition in 1.4) and leaves us with only a revocable, non-transferable licence expiring with the Order Form term. That fails the preferred position (we own what we pay for) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables: the 14.2 licence is revocable, term-limited and non-transferable, and the perpetual licence in 13.2 reaches only Vendor Technology/software embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself. The surrounding architecture is already at our preferred position, so the shortest complete fix is to reverse 14.2 alone: 14.1 confirms we own all Customer Data and our pre-existing IP, 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology for Vendor and routes embedded Vendor IP to the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence in 13.2, and 14.4 prevents joint ownership absent a signed instrument identifying exploitation rights. Our redline therefore only flips ownership of Deliverables and work product to us with a Vendor assignment; Vendor's platform and generic tools/know-how are untouched (1.4 and 1.8 expressly exclude them from Deliverables).

proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership in 14.2 to Customer, with Vendor assignment
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so we have reversed Section 14.2 to give us ownership of Deliverables and work product created for us, with an assignment from Vendor, in place of Vendor's exclusive ownership and the revocable, term-limited licence. Vendor still retains Vendor Technology under 14.3 and the perpetual paid-up licence in 13.2 continues to cover embedded Vendor IP; if Vendor must keep title, our fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Deliverables.

ops.newText: Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable and other work product created for Customer, and Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable and work product.

mappings.quote: As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.
